newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA V REAL BETIS STATISTICS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BARCELONA V REAL BETIS STATISTICS.

text.p: Facts and figures for the Spanish Cup final, Barcelona v Real Betis, at the Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid on Saturday.
Barcelona: Founded in 1899 by a Swiss resident in Barcelona, Hans Gamper.
Ground: Camp Nou (meaning the 'new ground' in the Catalan language, capacity 112,000. Coach: Bobby Robson (England).
Major honours: League champions: 1935. Spanish Cup winners: 1977.
Ground: Benito Villamarin, capacity 47,500. Coach: Lorenzo Serra Ferrer.

Barcelona's claret and blue colours are incorporated into the club shield alongside the red and yellow stripes of the Catalan Flag and the red cross of Sant Jordi, who appears in England as Saint George, slayer of dragons.
Real Betis's green and white striped shirts are supposed to represent the colours of the land in and around their native city of Seville and the Guadalquiver river which runs through it.

Barcelona have won both this season's games between the two teams: 3-0 at home and 4-2 away. Real Betis will compete in the Cup Winners' Cup next season regardless of the result. Barcelona finished second in the Spanish first division and gained entry to the UEFA Champions League. Real Betis finished fourth in the Spanish first division but lead the league back in September.
The two clubs have never met in the final before. If Barcelona win they will equal Athletic Bilbao's 23 victories in the competition, a Spanish Cup record.
